title: Lime and Cumin Steak Fajitas with Charred Peppers and Onions
summary: Skirt or flank steak marinates briefly in lime and cumin before being seared hot and sliced thin, served over smoky charred peppers and onions with warm tortillas.
equipment: large zip-lock bag or shallow dish
large cast-iron or heavy frying pan

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
red pepper, cut into 1 cm strips
yellow pepper, cut into 1 cm strips
green pepper, cut into 1 cm strips
large onion, halved and cut into 1 cm slices
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Whisk the marinade
steps.text: Whisk the lime juice, oil, garlic, cumin, chilli powder, sugar, salt and pepper together in the small bowl. Spoon 2 tbsp into a separate bowl for the vegetables before the mixture touches any raw meat, so there's no need to make a second batch later.

steps.title: Marinate the steak
steps.text: Put the steak in the bag or dish with the remaining marinade, turn to coat on all sides and refrigerate for 1-4 hours. Don't go beyond that window, as the lime juice's acidity starts to break down the surface texture and can leave the meat mushy rather than tender.

steps.title: Char the peppers and onion
steps.text: Toss the pepper strips and onion with the reserved marinade and salt. Heat the oil in the pan over medium-high heat and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened with patches of char, since those browned edges add a smoky sweetness steamed vegetables don't have.

steps.title: Finish and keep warm
steps.text: Stir half the coriander through the vegetables, then tip onto a platter and cover with foil. Trapping the steam this way keeps them hot without drying out while the steak cooks.

steps.title: Sear the steak
steps.text: Lift the steak from the marinade and discard the marinade, then pat the meat dry. Wipe out the pan, add the oil and heat over high heat until just smoking, and sear the steak for 3-5 minutes per side, cutting it into 2-3 pieces if it doesn't fit, until deeply browned and the thickest part reaches 63°C.

steps.title: Rest and slice against the grain
steps.text: Transfer the steak to the board and rest for at least 3 minutes before slicing thinly against the grain. Cutting across the fibres this way is what makes a cut like skirt or flank feel tender rather than chewy.

steps.title: Warm the tortillas
steps.text: Warm the tortillas in the dry pan for about 20 seconds per side until soft and pliable, then wrap in foil to keep them warm and stop them drying out before serving.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the sliced steak over the charred peppers and onions, scatter with the remaining coriander and bring to the table with the warm tortillas, soured cream and lime wedges for everyone to build their own.

tips: Common mistake: marinating the steak for too long. Stick to the 1-4 hour window, since the acidic lime juice will start to turn the surface mushy if left much longer.
Pat the steak properly dry before it hits the hot pan; a wet surface steams instead of browning, so you'll lose the deep sear.
Use an instant-read thermometer to check for 63°C in the thickest part rather than judging doneness by how the inside looks when cut.
Always rest the steak for at least 3 minutes before slicing, or the juices will run out onto the board instead of staying in the meat.
Cook the steak in batches if your pan isn't large enough to fit it in one layer; crowding it lowers the heat and stops it browning properly.
storage: Cool leftovers quickly, refrigerate within 1 hour, and use within 3 days; the cooked steak and vegetables also freeze well for up to 2 months, though tortillas are best bought fresh. Reheat gently in a pan or microwave until piping hot (74°C) before serving again. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
